title: The rotating walk check moves on through the set instead of re-running the same Ask walks every time
goal: The short walk check is meant to cover the whole set a chunk at a time, and for two weeks it re-ran the same slow Ask walks and hit its 30 minute limit. Since the check went to once every four hours it has stopped on the clock less, but one that does still starts over, and the printed schedule and the repo rules still describe checks after every task and a full run every day.
notes:
Reproduced in the 2026-10-26 digest pass. Commands and output:

$ cat queue/sweep/rotation.json -> "cursor": 103 (unchanged since the 11:51Z check on 2026-10-25)
$ grep '"ev":"slice_pass"' queue/history.jsonl | tail -3 -> 13:20Z walks 22 of 30 timedOut true; 15:43Z walks 21 timedOut true; 17:08Z walks 19 timedOut true, each seconds 1803-1806
$ grep -E '^[a-z0-9-]+-walk +[0-9]+s' queue/sweep/slice-2026-10-25-081308.log and -093850.log -> the same run every time: 3d-grippers-on-a-picked-layer-walk, an-editing-session-walk, arrow-*, then ask-adds-a-title-page-walk 82-93s, ask-annotates-a-screenshot-walk 80-105s, ask-builds-base-components-walk 206-303s, ask-cancels-a-waiting-request-walk 121-146s, ask-draws-a-dog-walk 151-183s, ask-draws-a-scene-walk 159-185s, ask-draws-an-illustration-walk 331-354s ...
$ grep 'Sized to' queue/loop.log | tail -1 -> 'Sized to 10 minutes at 19.8s a walk, the median of the last 10 rotating checks.'

Cause, read from code: queue/bin/sweep.sh around line 268 advances the rotation only when SLICE_TIMED_OUT is 0 ('a check cut off on the clock runs the same walks again next time rather than skipping them'), and queue/bin/sweep-schedule.mjs picks 30 walks from the median pace. From cursor 103 the next 30 walks hold about 20 Ask walks on the 27B model, so every check is stopped on the clock and the cursor never moves: a deadlock until the Ask walks get faster. ask-walks-share-one-model-instead-of-loading-a-f (one shared model) will shave the model load off each Ask walk but does not move the cursor, so this is its own fix. Do not let a fix skip walks nobody ran: advance only past finished walks.
acceptance: A check stopped on the clock moves the rotation past the walks it did finish, so the next check starts at the first walk it did not reach (a walk cut off part way runs again next time)

The check's size uses what the walks it is about to run have actually taken (each walk's own recent time where it has one), so a block of Ask walks at 100 to 350 s each is not sized at the 19.8 s median and the check ends inside its ten minutes instead of on the 30 minute clock

MEASURED: three rotating checks in a row through the Ask block (cursor near 103 today) each start further on than the last, none is stopped on the clock, and queue/sweep/rotation.json's cursor moves every time; the loop log lines are pasted in this task's log

The behaviour is held by queue/bin/sweep-schedule-drill.mjs (or a new drill beside it): a stopped check advances to its first unfinished walk, and a check made of slow walks is sized by their own times
The schedule text printed by queue/bin/sweep.sh schedule says what happens to a check stopped on the clock, in plain words

The schedule text and the repo rules say what the loop really does: the whole set at most every 72 hours, a rotating check at most every 4 hours, and how many days a lap of the set takes at that pace, read from the numbers
